title: Fallen Survey Line
description: A surviving foot and three split shaft drums along one fall line, ending in a broken cushion capital.

review.notes: New budget round 2 of 2 (last): rejected. Fixed: the pieces now run along one fall line from the surviving foot, a capital fragment ends the line, the turf is a strip with grass tufts and soil, and small shards lie between the pieces. Still failing: (1) silhouette/style 7: the drums still stand on their ends or edges at even spacing in one straight row, like a display, instead of lying on their sides rolled and partly sunk (hero, closeup). (2) form_detail 7: on the tilted drums the flutes read as horizontal stepped ribs, and the round drum reads as a gear wheel in profile; the break faces are flat, clean cuts (closeup centre). The capital is far wider than the foot and reads as an upturned flower pot or bucket, not a cushion capital under an abacus (closeup right, turn_155). (3) material 7: the stone shows mirror-like sky reflections on the break faces and the foot top (closeup centre, left), which reads as glossy plastic; the approved column weathering is barely visible. (4) defects 7: the broken flute stubs on top of the foot stand up like a crown. Fix: lay every drum on its side along the fall line, rolled to different angles, sunk 10-20 cm into soil with turf over the low side; keep the flutes running along each drum's axis; give the breaks a few large rough conchoidal planes with matte roughness; scale the capital to the column, with a square abacus over a curved echinus, one corner broken off; reuse the column's rain streaks and damp base; break the foot top into a low jagged stump.
